paper.title: FENICE: Factuality Evaluation of summarization based on Natural language Inference and Claim Extraction
paper.authors: Alessandro Scirè, Karim Ghonim, Roberto Navigli
paper.used: Section 4.4 (long-form evaluation, p. 14155-14156: 26 English narratives from Echoes from Alexandria, 12 Echo-XSum systems + references, 338 pairs, binary label, 80/20 val/test, annotation rule), Table 7 (balanced accuracy on the test split), Table 10 (66 factual / 273 not factual), Section 4.2 (threshold tuned on validation, Tang et al. 2023), Appendix A Fig. 2 (claim definition)
paper.parent_resource: https://github.com/Babelscape/echoes-from-alexandria @ f8abb6902dc7fcfbdb248da295876f4304cf654f (multilingual; only used to map narratives to Echo-XSum titles and for the Gutenberg cleaning rule)

release.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (dataset card; FENICE repo licence). Non-commercial redistribution with attribution under the same licence: summaries, labels and derived claims are frozen as JSONL.
release.fields: summary, factual (0/1), system_id (M0-M14, ref), text_id (Gutenberg id or Wikisource title), source (gutenberg|wikisource), id (= system_id_text_id; not unique)

gutenberg_hf.note: Named by the release card. Ids 697, 1472, 2165, 8164, 68377 are absent from it at every revision (single-commit upload 2023-09-07) and come from gutenberg.org instead.

gutenberg_org.note: current Project Gutenberg files; raw SHA-256 per file in data/frozen/fenice/narratives.json

story_texts.wikisource_pages: en.wikisource.org action=parse renders (revids in narratives.json) for sub-pages absent from the dump: 6 Thumbelina translations, The Liar (3 chapters) and A London Life (13 chapters) of the 1889 American-issue volume.
story_texts.licence: Public-domain literary texts (Project Gutenberg / Wikisource). Not stored in data/frozen: the script rebuilds them in data/raw; the adapter checks each document's SHA-256.

claim_extractor.settings: generation_config.json (num_beams 5, max_length 250), batch size 1, fp32 on CUDA, transformers 4.38.2, spaCy 3.7.4 en_core_web_sm 3.7.0 sentence split + de-duplication (FENICE ClaimExtractor.process_batch)

frozen.fields: id (<split>-<release line>), release_line, release_id, system_id, source, text_id, narrative, summary, claims, factual

test_n_resolution: The paper reports 26 narratives / 338 pairs (Table 10: 66 + 273 = 339) split 80/20 val/test without a test count. The release has 319 pairs with an explicit split: test 279 (49 factual / 230 non-factual), val 40 (10 / 30); 59/260 overall vs 66/273 in the paper. Narratives in the release: 25 (test 22 = 16 text_ids with Thumbelina x6 translations, A Tangled Tale x2 (byte-identical duplicate Gutenberg rows) ; val 3), vs 26 in the paper. We score the released test.jsonl (N = 279) as the paper's test split; 1 row is an exact duplicate of another (kept as released). The val split fixes the decision threshold as in the paper.

narrative_resolution.rule: row -> (source, text_id); the Henry James volume title maps to The Liar for all 16 test rows and A London Life for all 13 val rows (content: Oliver Lyon/Capadose vs Laura Wing; the refs match Echo-XSum 'The Liar' and 'A London Life').
narrative_resolution.wikisource_versions_pages: In wikimedia/wikisource 20231201.en the rows 'Thumbelina' (905 chars) and 'A London Life, The Patagonia, The Liar, Mrs. Temperly' (1,225 chars) are versions/disambiguation pages, not stories; the texts come from the rendered sub-pages.
narrative_resolution.thumbelina: 73 test rows (6 x 12 systems + 1 ref) share text_id 'Thumbelina' and repeat ids 6 times; the release does not say which of the six English Wikisource translations (Little Ellie, Little Tiny, Thumbeline, Tommelise, Thumbelina (Craigie), Thumbelisa; the Yellow Fairy Book one is gutenberg:640) each row summarises. Frozen rule: each claim is verified against all six translations and takes its best support. Reported separately: 'without_ambiguous_thumbelina' (N = 206).
narrative_resolution.stories_inside_collections: gutenberg:2814 is Dubliners but the narrative (ref = Echo-XSum 'The Dead'; all summaries about Gabriel/Morkans) is 'The Dead': section from the 'THE DEAD' heading to the end. gutenberg:640 is The Yellow Fairy Book, but all 12 summaries are about Thumbelina: section 'THUMBELINA' up to 'THE NIGHTINGALE'. Book-level narratives (Chronicles of Avonlea, My Man Jeeves, In a German Pension, A Tangled Tale, ...) use the whole book, as the Echo-XSum Wikipedia page is about the book.
narrative_resolution.cleaning: Gutenberg: Echoes-from-Alexandria clean_text (drop [Illustration]/[Footnote] notes, keep text between START/END markers); all texts NFC, LF, trailing spaces stripped, 3+ newlines collapsed. Wikisource: rendered HTML minus header/noexport/page-number/hidden nodes, block text joined by blank lines.

english_verification.metadata: Paper: '26 English narratives'; dataset card language: en; texts from English Gutenberg/Wikisource.
english_verification.method: langid (all languages) on all 319 summaries and on every paragraph >= 200 chars of every story document, plus Latin-script share; flags inspected. Report: data/raw/fenice/english_report.json (rebuilt by the script).
english_verification.result: 5 summary flags (et/nb/de/de/mt), all short English headline-style strings: "CNN 20: Tommelise's Wife Speaks Out", 'All photographs  Kjell Nedrelid.', 'CNN 20: Tiny Thumb Marries Uglier Toad', 'CNN 20: Oliver Lyon Dies, June 23, 1997', 'A TANGLED TALE BY LEWIS CARROLL'. All 24 story documents: whole-text langid en, Latin share >= 0.99, 0 non-English paragraphs. No rows dropped.

request_design.primitive: noul per claim; all claims of one summary share one request per source chunk
request_design.chunking: MAX_CHUNK_CHARS 72,000 (frozen, src/gauntlet/tasks/fenice.py); documents up to 362K chars -> up to 6 parts; nothing truncated

metric.primary: balanced accuracy on test, threshold tuned on released val via FENICE eval/aggrefact.py choose_best_threshold (percentiles 0..99.8 step 0.2 of val scores; factual iff score > threshold)
secondary: balanced accuracy at a fixed 0.5 threshold
both on the 206 test rows outside the ambiguous Thumbelina narrative

deviations: Test N = 279 released rows (val 40), not a count derivable from the paper's 338 pairs; the release has 319 pairs and 25 identifiable narratives.
Claims: FENICE_T5_claims extractor (released); the GPT-3.5 claims behind the paper's best number (66.2) are not released. Comparison target: FENICE_T5_claims 65.7.

Story texts rebuilt from public sources; the release gives only ids. 5 Gutenberg ids missing from manu/project_gutenberg are taken from gutenberg.org (current files). Wikisource sub-pages are current renders (revids recorded); annotators read PDFs of unknown edition.
Thumbelina (73 test rows): source translation unidentified; claims verified against all six candidate translations (max). Sensitivity subset without them reported.
Two narratives inside collections use the story section (The Dead; Thumbelina in The Yellow Fairy Book).
Long stories are split into <=72,000-char parts and a claim's score is its max over parts (FENICE's own max-over-passages alignment, Eq. 2); Jev never sees the whole of a >72K-char story at once.
Jev's per-claim P(supported) replaces FENICE's NLI entailment-minus-contradiction score (range [0,1] vs [-1,1]); the val-tuned threshold absorbs the scale.
